name: Mamluk Iraq
alt: Mamluk pashaliks of Baghdad, Basra and Shahrizor

predecessors.name: Ottoman Empire
predecessors.text: the Ottoman pashalik of Baghdad, to which Basra came 'from around 1705' (Ottoman Iraq page); the Baghdad, Basra, Mosul and Shahrizor eyalets had been separate Ottoman units

successors.name: Ottoman Empire
successors.text: Baghdad, Basra and Shahrizor, 'brought under direct Ottoman rule' after Dawud Pasha's dismissal in 1831 (Ottoman Iraq page)

rulers.name: Sulayman the Little (son of Sulayman the Great)
rulers.title: Pasha of Baghdad

rulers.name: Said Pasha (son of Sulayman the Great)
rulers.title: Pasha of Baghdad

ledger.x: 1704: Hasan Pasha begins the Mamluk line at Baghdad.

c. 1705: Basra comes under Baghdad's control. The Ottoman Iraq page: 'Basra came under Baghdad's control from around 1705'; the Mamluk dynasty page has Sulayman Abu Layla 'brought Basra under their control' with no year.
20 April 1776: Basra falls to the Zands.
28 July 1823: the Treaty of Erzurum restores the old frontier.
1831: the sultan's army marches on Baghdad.

wars.name: Persian attack on Iraq of 1733
wars.outcome: Nader Shah's forces attacked Erbil and Kirkuk; Topal Osman Pasha defeated them near Baghdad but was killed near Kirkuk and Kirkuk capitulated; Mosul's governor repelled a six-day siege.

wars.name: Siege of Basra (1775-1776)
wars.outcome: Sadeq Khan Zand besieged Basra from 6 April 1775; the Ottoman garrison surrendered on 20 April 1776.

wars.name: Wahhabi raids on Najaf and Hillah
wars.outcome: Ali al-Kahiya 'repelled raids on Najaf and Hillah' in 1803 and 1806 but 'failed to challenge their domination of the desert'.

wars.name: Ottoman-Persian War (1821-1823)
wars.outcome: Dawud Pasha invaded Iran and failed; Mohammad-Ali Mirza 'took Shahrezur, conquered Sulaymaniyah, and besieged Baghdad' until cholera lifted the siege.

wars.name: Ottoman campaign against Dawud Pasha
wars.outcome: The sultan decreed Dawud's dismissal in 1830; his emissary was executed; Ali Riza Pasha marched from Aleppo in 1831 and Baghdad capitulated after a ten-week blockade.

certainty.note: The Iraqi desert west of the Euphrates, the Kurdish hills and the Muntafiq marshes are approximate.
